Krusader 2.6.0 hands the screen size back to you. Version 2.5.0 capped it at 5120x2880 to save memory, which was the wrong place to make that decision: a size baked into the image is the one thing a user cannot undo. The full range is available again, and the template now lets you pick or type whatever you want.

## ✨ Added

- **A screen-size dropdown with the cost written on it.** `MAX_RES` lists sizes from 1080p up to the full 15360x8640, each entry labelled with the memory it needs, so the trade is visible while you choose rather than buried in a wiki page.
- **A free field for anything not in the list.** `MAX_RES_CUSTOM` takes any `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, for example `3440x1440` or `6016x3384`, and wins over the dropdown when you fill it in. Two fields rather than one editable dropdown because Unraid renders any variable with preset values as a plain select with no way to type into it.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The full resolution is the default again.** Nothing is capped unless you ask for it. The container idles around 700 MB that way, and picking a preset brings it down: roughly 295 MB at 4K, 210 MB at 3440x1440, 200 MB at 1080p. All measured on a live container.
- **A typo cannot take the desktop down.** The screen size goes straight to the X server as a command line argument, so `1920*1080` would have stopped it from starting and left you with no desktop and no hint why. Such a value is now ignored with a line in the container log, and the next usable setting applies. That includes sizes that merely look plausible: `15360x86400` would ask for a five gigabyte framebuffer and be killed on every boot, so each side is bounded at 16384, which sits above the largest preset.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A rejected screen size can no longer reach the X server anyway.** Docker environment variables are imported into the service environment before any of this runs, so an unusable value was sitting there already and would have been used despite the fallback. It is now removed, which is what makes the fallback real.

*Upgrading:* the two fields appear in the Unraid template after it refreshes. If you liked 2.5.0's smaller footprint, pick `5120x2880` from the dropdown and you are back where you were.
